This evidence prioritizes fuel/context dependency and code placement among remaining investigation targets. It does not prove instruction-cache/branch-predictor misses or a causal regression mechanism. The rejected candidate still must not be adopted.

causalFrontier.proven: Same frozen workload/native/expectedresult/fuel; hot sampled original instruction regions and exact mappings; no static fusion/frame inflation.
causalFrontier.unproven: Why equivalent smaller clone CALL spans are slower. Address-dependent instruction fetch/prediction and context dependency latency remain hypotheses requiring a separately preregistered diagnostic/control or hardware counters.

limitations: SIGPROF records interrupted PCs, not instruction retirement, cycles, cache misses or branch mispredictions. Saved PC may be next instruction after an asynchronous stall/interrupt. No elapsed measurement statistics are analyzed or pooled.

Timer delivery is scheduler/coalescing dependent; proportions and per-run ranges are reported, and capture counts are not speed ratios. Two intervals/order reversal reduce but do not prove elimination of periodic alias bias.

Host metadata includes before/after uname/cpu/load plus per-run load; profiles required load<3. No host_processor_info CPU tick envelope or scheduling trace was recorded, so no quiet-host performance qualification is claimed.

Each of8processes bounded45seconds, capture65536entries, wholejob420seconds. Actual no dropped samples. Driver restores original SIGPROF action/timer/mask and drains pending tick after disabling; no loader SIGILL/SIGTRAP handlers overwritten.
